newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks register slowdown in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks register slowdown in thin trade.

text.p: Cyprus stocks dropped slightly on Friday at the end of an uneventful week of listless trading but things should pick up soon, traders said.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index, set at 100 points, closed at 82.21 points on Friday, declining 0.97 percent from its close of 83.02 last week.
"We should start seeing a reversal in the levels of the index around the second week of December," said Nicos Severis, chairman of brokers Sigma-Severis and Athientis Ltd in Nicosia.

"There is a vested interest by some institutions to see higher prices before some companies close their books on December 31 and they will do that by moving into the market on a buying spree," he said.

CISCO, the Cyprus Investments and Securities Corporation, said in its weekly report that prices in sectors like banking were falling because institutional investors were realising a large percentage of their profits before the end of the year.
"It is also possible that part of the cash raised is to be channelled towards new issues in the market," it said.
The Bank of Cyprus on Thursday opened its registry for the issue of 10 million pounds ($21.95 million) worth of subordinated convertible bonds. The registry closes on December 2.
Later Friday the second largest banking instutution, the Cyprus Popular Bank, will announce its own issue of convertible bonds worth 15 million pounds.
The banking sub-index, the strongest on the market, closed at 91.04 points on Friday from 91.71 on Friday.

Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed at 339.5, down four cents from last week's close of 343.5. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 330, down by half a cent from last week.
The third largest bank, the Hellenic Bank closed higher at 267 from 265.5 last week. Universal Savings Bank Savings Bank closed at 135, down one cent from Friday.
The sub index in the insurance sector went down by 52 basis points to close at 75.32.
Shares in Universal Life closed at 382 from 384 on Friday. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid closed at 129 from 133.5 last week.
Interamerican Insurance closed at 102.5, down half a cent. Associate company Philiki Insurance closed at 243, up 4.5 cents from last week.
Cement producer Vassiliko closed up one cent at 154.5. Keo, the Cypriot beer and wine producer, closed at 108 from 109 last week.
National carrier Cyprus Airways was trading at 39.9 cents on Friday from last week's close of 41 cents. ($=0.455 pounds)
